study: Miller/Biggart/Sloan/O'Hare 2017 — EEF Success for All (SfA) effectiveness trial
eval_evidence: EEF-commissioned effectiveness trial; independent evaluators = Centre for Evidence and Social Innovation, Queen's University Belfast (Miller et al.). No developer stake in the evaluation.
developer_evidence: PD delivered by the Success for All Foundation (program developers): 'Initial training is delivered by SfA-UK'; SfA trainers provided training, coaching, co-teaching and staff meetings to schools.
cascade_evidence: SfA Foundation trainers train the school's teachers and TAs directly ('Delivered by 3 SfA trainers to the whole school'; teachers/TAs 'trained and supported by the Success for All Foundation') — no intermediary hop.
counterfactual_evidence: Control schools 'continued with business as usual which consisted of curriculum delivery as normal' (paid GBP2000/yr); no alternative literacy program supplied.
coaching_evidence: SfA provides 16 days of in-school training plus 'ongoing support', including coaching and co-teaching in classrooms across the 2-year rollout — recurring in-class support.
student_dose_evidence: Whole-school literacy program restructures the teacher's regular daily instruction (group learning, phonics, structured lessons); the evaluated Reception->Year 1 cohort receives no separate student-facing pull-out/tutoring dose reported in this trial.
maturity_evidence: Schools were new adopters; SfA delivered over 2 years and pupils were followed from the start of Reception (first implementation year for these schools/teachers).
